A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 20-page versions of LLaVA-ReID. Their main sections, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original interactive retrieval experiments, integration with text-based ReID methods, and selection ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised numerical entries in the selection ablation table.

M1.justification: The Retriever–Questioner–Answerer framework, candidate selector, looking-forward supervision, and training objectives remain unchanged. The corresponding architecture and prompts in the appendices are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use Interactive-PEDES and evaluate integration on CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, and RSTPReid. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SimIRV, ChatIR, and PlugIR. Table 2 retains CFine, RaSa, APTM, AUL, IRRA, and RDE, and Table 3 retains the same selection comparators.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, four selected candidates, five interaction rounds, training settings, and Recall/mAP/BRI metrics are unchanged. The revised Table 3 values are not accompanied by any reported protocol change.

E4.justification: Both retain the same candidate-selection and question-selection ablations, Appendix A dataset analyses, and qualitative cases in Figures 7–8. Table 3 has numerical revisions, but no analytical question or test is added or redesigned.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, performance uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises all six BRI entries, including selector and look-forward from 1.041 to 0.719 and random question selection from 1.173 to 0.813. Uniform selection's R@5 changes from 90.00 to 90.06. Rankings and the results in Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 remain unchanged; the revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: The task definitions and Equations 1–10, including selection probabilities, the question-selection rule, and the NLL objective, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both claim a new interactive person re-identification task and dataset, a selective multi-image questioner, and benefits for interactive and text-based ReID. The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: The candidate-selection rationale, interpretations of experimental results, limitation concerning dialogue-based retrieval, and privacy and surveillance concerns are retained without substantive changes.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain the same construction and inference prompts, architecture details, hyperparameters, training schedules, hardware, and metric descriptions. The code repository link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Gong et al. (2022), Ding et al. (2025), and Lin et al. (2023). These are limited citation additions without substantial changes to research positioning or evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v3 makes small wording and grammatical edits and adds acknowledgments and publication metadata. The main narrative, section order, and appendix text remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds running headers and a conference footer, updates Figure 1's questioner icons, slightly resizes Figure 4, and moves Table 3 to the right column with an expanded caption. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Table 3's full-model BRI now matches Table 1 at 0.719, replacing 1.041 and resolving an internal reporting inconsistency. Together with modest presentation refinements, this provides a limited quality improvement. The numerical revisions remain unexplained, and the scientific evidence and central claims are otherwise unchanged.
